baseline.label: Long-run baseline
baseline.note: Inflation is the 1913-2026 compound average of the CPI-U, computed on this desk from the BLS series. House growth and equity return are planning assumptions shown as a range, not forecasts.

deflation_1930s.label: Deflation: the 1929-1933 record
deflation_1930s.note: Inflation is the actual CPI-U compound rate from 1929 to 1933, computed on this desk (index 17.16 to 12.93 = -6.85% a year). The Dow's -89% drawdown over the same period is from Federal Reserve History. The house and equity paths are assumptions that reproduce that record.

great_recession.label: Credit shock: the 2007-2009 record
great_recession.note: Federal Reserve History: the S&P 500 fell 57% from October 2007 to March 2009 and home prices about 30% from mid-2006 to mid-2009. The annual rates used here are assumptions that reproduce those cumulative moves over three years.

high_inflation.label: High inflation: the 1972-1982 record
high_inflation.note: Inflation is the actual CPI-U compound rate from 1972 to 1982, computed on this desk (index 41.82 to 96.50 = 8.72% a year). House and equity growth in that decade are assumptions; both are set below inflation because real returns were poor.

stagnation.label: Low growth: no crash and no boom
stagnation.note: A deliberately dull regime, assumption only, included so the comparison is not decided by one optimistic path.
